experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex Tour
experiences.description: Explore the largest ancient castle complex in the world, including St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Walk through centuries of Bohemian history and enjoy panoramic views over Prague's red rooftops and the Vltava River.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in one of Europe's largest and most iconic thermal bath complexes, built in 1913 in stunning Neo-Baroque style. Enjoy indoor and outdoor pools fed by natural hot springs, a quintessential Budapest cultural tradition dating back to Ottoman rule.

experiences.name: Old Town Prague Food & History Walking Tour
experiences.description: Wander through Prague's medieval Old Town Square, visit the famous Astronomical Clock, and sample traditional Czech street food including trdelník, svíčková, and local craft beer. A guided walk blending culinary delights with rich historical storytelling.

experiences.name: Buda Castle Hill & Hungarian National History Walk
experiences.description: Climb or take the historic funicular up Castle Hill to explore Buda Castle, Matthias Church, and the Fisherman's Bastion. Discover over 1,000 years of Hungarian history while enjoying breathtaking views across the Danube to Pest.

experiences.name: Danube River Evening Cruise
experiences.description: Sail along the Danube at sunset and after dark to witness Budapest's UNESCO-listed skyline illuminated, including the Hungarian Parliament Building, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle. An unforgettable way to absorb the grandeur of the city from the water.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Václav Havel Airport Prague at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly Airport Express bus (Line AE) to Hlavní nádraží (Main Train Station) for ~60 CZK (~$2.50). Check into hostel/budget accommodation in central Prague. Grab a late-night snack near the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Late-night kebab or convenience store near accommodation (~100-150 CZK / ~$4-6)

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy for tomorrow. Exchange some currency at the airport (small amount) or use a no-fee ATM. Avoid taxi touts — use official taxis or rideshare apps like Bolt.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a free self-guided walking tour of Prague Old Town (Staré Město). Visit the iconic Old Town Square, watch the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) strike the hour at 9:00 AM, and admire the Týn Church exterior. Grab a cheap breakfast at a local bakery (pekárna).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the historic Charles Bridge (free, best explored on foot) and climb up to Prague Castle (Hradčany). Explore the castle grounds — the exterior and St. Vitus Cathedral courtyard are free. Pay for select interior attractions if budget allows (~250 CZK / ~$11 for Circuit B). Stroll through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhood for an authentic local dinner. Explore the lively bar scene on Náměstí Míru square. Try a local Czech pub for the evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Pekárna (local bakery) — pastry + coffee (~80 CZK / ~$3.50)
meals.lunch: Lokál or similar Czech pub — svíčková (beef sirloin) or guláš with bread (~180 CZK / ~$8)
meals.dinner: Budget Czech restaurant in Žižkov — roast pork, dumplings, sauerkraut + local Pilsner (~200 CZK / ~$9)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Prague's cobblestones are tough on feet. Download the Prague Public Transport app (PID) for easy navigation. A 24-hour transit pass costs ~120 CZK (~$5.50).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Vyšehrad Fortress (free entry to grounds) — a less-touristy historic citadel with stunning panoramic views over the Vltava River. Explore the Vyšehrad Cemetery where famous Czech figures are buried. Peaceful and uncrowded compared to Prague Castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take tram to the Josefov (Jewish Quarter). Walk through the exterior of the historic synagogues and Jewish Town Hall (combined museum ticket ~550 CZK / ~$25 if budget allows, or admire exteriors for free). Head to Letná Park for sweeping city views and a beer at the famous Letná Beer Garden (~50-60 CZK per beer).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Nusle or Holešovice neighborhood for street art and local culture. Visit a local farmers' market if available. Enjoy dinner at a local pivnice (beer hall).

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at a café near accommodation (~90 CZK / ~$4)
meals.lunch: Street food — trdelník (chimney cake) + sausage near Old Town (~100 CZK / ~$4.50)
meals.dinner: Pivnice U Fleků or similar traditional beer hall — pork knee or schnitzel (~250 CZK / ~$11)

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is a hidden gem — arrive early to enjoy the peaceful atmosphere. The Letná Beer Garden is cash only. September weather in Prague is mild (~15-20°C / 59-68°F), so bring a light jacket for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning to revisit favorite spots or explore the Nové Město (New Town) area. Visit Wenceslas Square — the heart of modern Prague with significant historical importance. Check out the National Museum (exterior, or entry ~200 CZK / ~$9). Pack bags and check out of Prague accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the budget train or FlixBus from Prague to Budapest (approximately 6-7 hours, from ~$15-25 USD booked in advance via Regiojet or FlixBus). Depart around 13:00-14:00 from Praha Hlavní nádraží. Enjoy the scenic countryside views through the Czech and Slovak/Hungarian landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Budapest Keleti or Déli train station (~19:00-21:00). Take Metro Line M2 or M4 to central accommodation (~350 HUF / ~$1). Check in to Budapest budget hostel. Take a short evening stroll along the Danube embankment to see the illuminated Parliament Building.

meals.breakfast: Quick grab-and-go at Prague bakery before checkout (~90 CZK / ~$4)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or train station sandwich for the journey (~150 CZK / ~$7)
meals.dinner: Lángos (Hungarian fried dough) from a street vendor near Keleti station or ruin bar area (~1,500 HUF / ~$4)

day_by_day.notes: Book Prague–Budapest transport in advance for best prices. Regiojet offers comfortable buses/trains with WiFi and free drinks on some routes. Validate your Budapest transit ticket immediately upon boarding — inspectors are strict.

day_by_day.morning: Start with Budapest's crown jewel — the Hungarian Parliament Building. Admire the exterior from the Danube bank (free) or book a guided interior tour (~8,900 HUF / ~$24 for non-EU citizens — worth it!). Walk through Kossuth Lajos Square and explore the surrounding government district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Chain Bridge on foot to the Buda side. Hike or take the funicular (~1,300 HUF / ~$3.50) up Castle Hill to Buda Castle and the Royal Palace. Explore Matthias Church and Fisherman's Bastion (exterior free, interior tower ~1,500 HUF / ~$4). Enjoy panoramic views over Pest from the bastion.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the famous ruin bar district in the Jewish Quarter (VII. district). Visit Szimpla Kert — Budapest's most iconic ruin bar. Enjoy cheap craft beers (~900-1,200 HUF / ~$2.50-3.50) and soak in the eclectic atmosphere. Saturday night is lively here.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud or local café near accommodation — coffee + pastry (~1,500 HUF / ~$4)
meals.lunch: Halászbástya area — packed lunch or grab goulash soup from a local eatery (~2,000 HUF / ~$5.50)
meals.dinner: Karavan Street Food Court near Szimpla Kert — burgers, langos, or international street food (~2,500 HUF / ~$7)

day_by_day.notes: Szimpla Kert also hosts a Sunday farmers' market if you're there the next morning. Wear comfortable shoes for the Castle Hill cobblestones. The Budapest Card (~24-hour version, ~6,900 HUF / ~$19) may be worth it for heavy transit users.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — Budapest's stunning 19th-century iron market hall. Browse fresh produce, paprika, Hungarian salami, and handcrafts on the ground floor. It's free to enter and a fantastic cultural experience. Pick up budget souvenirs here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Jewish Quarter and the magnificent Dohány Street Synagogue — the largest in Europe (~6,000 HUF / ~$16.50 entry, includes museum). Walk through the Emanuel Tree memorial and the Jewish cemetery within the complex. Stroll through Erzsébetváros (VII. district) and admire street art.
day_by_day.evening: Take a budget Danube evening walk along the Pest embankment. Visit the haunting Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial (free) — a powerful Holocaust memorial. Watch the Parliament and Chain Bridge light up at dusk. Grab dinner in the IX. district (Ferencváros) — a trendy, more local area.

meals.breakfast: Market Hall — fresh bread, cheese, and cold cuts from vendors (~1,500 HUF / ~$4)
meals.lunch: Főzelékfaló Ételbár — traditional Hungarian vegetable stew bar, very cheap and local (~2,000 HUF / ~$5.50)
meals.dinner: Menza or similar retro-style Hungarian restaurant in Ferencváros — goulash, pörkölt, or stuffed peppers (~3,500 HUF / ~$9.50)

day_by_day.notes: The Great Market Hall is busiest on Saturday mornings — Sunday is calmer. Bargain respectfully at souvenir stalls on the upper floor. The Shoes on the Danube memorial is most atmospheric at dusk or dawn.

day_by_day.morning: Experience Budapest's legendary thermal bath culture. Visit Széchenyi Thermal Bath in City Park — one of the largest and most beautiful in Europe (~8,500 HUF / ~$23 for cabin + locker, weekday morning is less crowded). Spend 2-3 hours soaking in the outdoor and indoor pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Városliget (City Park) — free to wander. Visit the Vajdahunyad Castle exterior (free) and Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) with the Millennium Monument (free). If budget allows, visit the Museum of Fine Arts (~3,200 HUF / ~$8.50). Stroll down Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's grand boulevard, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.evening: Take Metro M1 (the oldest underground railway in continental Europe) down Andrássy Avenue. Explore the Opera House exterior (free) or book a budget evening tour (~3,500 HUF / ~$9.50). Head to the Gozsdu Udvar courtyard — a string of interconnected courtyards packed with bars and restaurants — for a final festive Budapest evening.

meals.breakfast: Grab pastry and coffee near accommodation before the baths (~1,200 HUF / ~$3.50)
meals.lunch: City Park kiosk or packed lunch — lángos or sandwich (~1,800 HUF / ~$5)
meals.dinner: Gozsdu Udvar — choose from multiple vendors; try kürtőskalács (chimney cake) for dessert (~3,000 HUF / ~$8)

day_by_day.notes: Book Széchenyi Baths online in advance to save time and sometimes money. Bring flip-flops and a swimsuit. Lockers are mandatory. The thermal waters are rich in minerals and genuinely relaxing — a true Budapest bucket-list experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit Gellért Hill for the best panoramic views of the city (free hike, ~20-30 minutes up). See the Citadella fortress and the Liberty Statue at the top. A perfect spot for final photos of the Danube, bridges, and both Buda and Pest stretching into the horizon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back down and explore the Gellért Baths exterior (one of Budapest's most ornate Art Nouveau buildings). Browse any remaining souvenir shopping along Váci Street or the Market Hall. Pack bags, check out of accommodation, and make your way to Budapest Liszt Ferenc International Airport (BUD) via Bus 100E from Deák Ferenc tér (~900 HUF / ~$2.50, direct airport bus).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Budapest or continue onward travel. Reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most beautiful and historically rich capitals.

meals.breakfast: Final Hungarian breakfast — ham, cheese, eggs at a local café (Retró Büfé style) (~1,500 HUF / ~$4)
meals.lunch: Quick and hearty — kürtős (chimney cake) + coffee or a wrap near the city center (~1,800 HUF / ~$5)
meals.dinner: Airport or departure point — budget airport sandwich/meal (~3,000-4,000 HUF / ~$8-11)

day_by_day.notes: Bus 100E is the cheapest and most direct airport connection — runs every 20-30 minutes and takes ~35 minutes to the airport. Arrive at the airport at least 2 hours before departure. Consider picking up a bottle of Unicum (Hungarian herbal liqueur) or Tokaji wine as a budget-friendly souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Prague Václav Havel Airport at 22:30. Take the Airport Express bus or a pre-booked taxi to your accommodation in central Prague. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented. Pick up a city map at the hotel reception.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night bite near the hotel — try a 24-hour Czech pub for a bowl of svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) or a simple open-faced chlebíček sandwich from a nearby deli if available

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 completely relaxed. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements in advance as arrival is late at 22:30. Exchange some currency or withdraw Czech Koruna (CZK) from an ATM at the airport. Rest well — big days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a leisurely walk through Prague's UNESCO-listed Old Town Square. Marvel at the medieval Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and watch the hourly mechanical show. Explore the Gothic Týn Church and the Baroque St. Nicholas Church. Stroll across the cobblestoned square and soak in the architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the Josefov Jewish Quarter — one of the best-preserved Jewish districts in Europe. Visit the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Pinkas Synagogue (a Holocaust memorial), and the Spanish Synagogue with its stunning Moorish interior. Combo tickets are available at the entrance for mid-range budgets.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the iconic Charles Bridge at golden hour for stunning views over the Vltava River. Browse the bridge's Baroque statues as the sun sets. Head to the Malá Strana (Lesser Town) side for a relaxed evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre or a local bakery near Old Town — try a fresh koláč (Czech pastry) with coffee
meals.lunch: Lokál Dlouhááá — a beloved mid-range Czech beer hall serving authentic svíčková, goulash, and tank-fresh Pilsner Urquell
meals.dinner: Café Savoy in Malá Strana — elegant yet mid-range, serving Czech and European classics in a stunning neo-Renaissance interior

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Jewish Quarter combo ticket costs approximately 350–500 CZK. Book dinner reservations at Café Savoy in advance as it fills up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Devote the morning to Prague Castle — the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral (a Gothic masterpiece), the Royal Palace, the Golden Lane (a charming row of medieval cottages), and the Basilica of St. George. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the castle through the picturesque Nerudova Street back into Malá Strana. Take a tram to the hip Vinohrady neighborhood. Explore its Art Nouveau apartment buildings, boutique shops, and the peaceful Riegrovy Sady park with panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Prague's emerging food and craft beer scene in Vinohrady. Visit a local craft brewery or wine bar for an evening of tasting and relaxation.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a local pekárna (bakery) for fresh bread rolls and coffee
meals.lunch: Malostranska Beseda — a mid-range restaurant near the castle with Czech cuisine and live folk music atmosphere
meals.dinner: Eska in Žižkov (nearby neighborhood) — a celebrated modern Czech restaurant focusing on fermentation and local ingredients; mid-range to slightly upscale but worth it

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle tickets range from 250–350 CZK depending on the circuit chosen. Opt for the 'Long Circuit' to see the most. Trams are cheap and efficient — get a 24-hour pass for around 120 CZK.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final morning in Prague. Take a relaxed walk along the Vltava riverbanks or revisit Charles Bridge one more time without the afternoon crowds. Pick up some Czech souvenirs — Bohemian crystal, Becherovka liqueur, or local honey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of your Prague accommodation and travel to Budapest. The most scenic and recommended option is the RegioJet or FlixBus train/bus (approximately 6–7 hours, very affordable at €15–30). Alternatively, a flight takes only 1 hour but adds airport time. Arrive in Budapest in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Check into your Budapest accommodation. Take a gentle orientation walk along the Danube embankment at night — the illuminated Parliament Building and Chain Bridge are breathtaking. Get your first feel for the Hungarian capital.

meals.breakfast: Final Czech breakfast at your Prague hotel or a café near the departure point
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a Prague deli or grab food at the bus/train station for the journey
meals.dinner: Borkonyha Winekitchen in Budapest — a Michelin-starred restaurant that remains mid-range by local standards, specializing in Hungarian wines and creative Hungarian cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague–Budapest transport in advance. RegioJet is highly recommended for comfort and value. Store luggage at Budapest Keleti station if you arrive before hotel check-in. Budapest uses Hungarian Forint (HUF) — withdraw cash upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Cross the Chain Bridge and ascend Castle Hill by funicular or on foot. Explore Buda Castle (the Royal Palace), now home to the Hungarian National Gallery and the Budapest History Museum. Walk through the medieval Fisherman's Bastion for panoramic views over the Danube and Pest side.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Matthias Church — a Gothic-Baroque masterpiece at the heart of the Castle District. Descend back to Pest and spend the afternoon at the legendary Széchenyi Thermal Bath — a grand Neo-Baroque spa complex. Soak in the outdoor pools and indoor thermal baths.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Jewish Quarter in Pest (District VII). Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street — the largest synagogue in Europe. Stroll through the Gozsdu Courtyard, a lively passage filled with bars, restaurants, and street food.

meals.breakfast: New York Café or a local pékség (bakery) — try a kürtőskalács (chimney cake) from a street vendor near the castle
meals.lunch: Café Pierrot in the Castle District — charming mid-range café with Hungarian classics in a romantic setting
meals.dinner: Mazel Tov in the Jewish Quarter — a stunning open-air restaurant in a ruined courtyard serving Middle Eastern–inspired dishes; lively and mid-range

day_by_day.notes: Széchenyi Bath entry costs approximately 5,000–7,000 HUF. Bring a swimsuit and a towel or rent one on-site. The Great Synagogue charges an entry fee of around 4,000 HUF and includes a Holocaust memorial garden.

day_by_day.date: 2027-09-20 (Sunday) — Budapest: Parliament, Andrássy Avenue & Heroes' Square
day_by_day.morning: Join a guided tour of the Hungarian Parliament Building — one of the most magnificent legislative buildings in the world. Pre-book tickets online (approximately 6,000 HUF for non-EU visitors). Afterwards, walk along the Danube Promenade and visit the haunting Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll up the grand Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's answer to the Champs-Élysées and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House (exterior or guided tour). Continue to the end of the avenue to reach Heroes' Square and the Millennium Monument. Explore City Park (Városliget) and Vajdahunyad Castle.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's famous ruin bar culture. Visit Szimpla Kert — the original and most iconic ruin bar — for craft beers, cocktails, and a uniquely eclectic atmosphere in a crumbling courtyard building.

meals.breakfast: Centrál Kávéház — a grand historic coffee house on Károlyi Street; try lángos (deep-fried dough) from a nearby market stall
meals.lunch: Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — a legendary Budapest institution for cakes, coffee, and light lunch; mid-range
meals.dinner: Menza on Liszt Ferenc Square — a stylish retro-socialist-themed restaurant serving elevated Hungarian comfort food at mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be pre-booked at least 1–2 days in advance at the official website. Sunday mornings are great for visiting markets — check out the Hold Street Market for fresh local produce and street food.

day_by_day.morning: Take a leisurely morning on Margaret Island — a peaceful green oasis in the middle of the Danube. Rent a bicycle or take a tourist train around the island. Visit the medieval monastery ruins, the Musical Fountain, and the Japanese Garden. Perfect for a slower-paced cultural morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a Danube River cruise for a 1–2 hour sightseeing experience on the water. See the Parliament, Buda Castle, Chain Bridge, and Fisherman's Bastion from a completely different perspective. Several operators offer afternoon departures at mid-range prices (approximately 4,000–6,000 HUF).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center for a final evening of exploration. Visit the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) for last-minute souvenir shopping — pick up paprika, Tokaji wine, embroidered textiles, and Hungarian salami. End the evening with a sunset walk across the Chain Bridge.

meals.breakfast: A relaxed breakfast at your hotel or a nearby neighborhood café
meals.lunch: Picnic on Margaret Island from supplies bought at a local market or supermarket — great way to enjoy the greenery
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown — a sophisticated yet accessible fine-dining experience for a special final-night Budapest dinner; slightly above mid-range but ideal for a celebratory meal

day_by_day.notes: Margaret Island is free to enter. Bicycle rentals cost approximately 1,000–2,000 HUF per hour. Book the Danube cruise in advance online for better pricing. The Great Market Hall closes by 17:00 on weekdays and earlier on Sundays — plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final relaxed morning in Budapest. Revisit a favorite spot or explore a neighborhood you haven't seen yet — the bohemian Ferencváros (District IX) with its galleries and design shops is a great option. Stop for one last Hungarian coffee and pastry at a local kávéház.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of your accommodation and head to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (approximately 30 minutes by taxi or the 100E airport bus from Deák Ferenc Square at about 900 HUF). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry wonderful memories of Prague's Gothic spires and Budapest's grand boulevards home with you.

meals.breakfast: A final Hungarian breakfast — try rántotta (scrambled eggs) or túrós táska (cottage cheese pastry) at a local café
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a sandwich from a bakery near your hotel before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Keep some HUF for the airport bus or a small tip. Duty-free shopping at Budapest Airport offers Hungarian specialties like Unicum liqueur and Tokaji wine at reasonable prices. Confirm your flight details and any baggage requirements the evening before departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Travel Day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Travel Day
day_by_day.evening: Arrival at Václav Havel Airport Prague at 22:30 on flight UA. A pre-arranged luxury private transfer (Mercedes-Benz S-Class or equivalent) whisks you to your hotel in the heart of Prague. Check in, unwind with a welcome amenity, and enjoy a late-night nightcap at the hotel bar.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at origin airport
meals.lunch: In-flight or at origin airport
meals.dinner: Late-night room service or hotel bar charcuterie & wine selection upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is at 22:30 – no activities scheduled before check-in. Confirm private transfer with your concierge in advance. Keep the evening light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a gourmet breakfast at the hotel. At 10:00, embark on a private guided walking tour of Prague's UNESCO-listed Old Town (Staré Město). Explore the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) on Old Town Square, admire the Gothic spires of the Church of Our Lady before Týn, and stroll through the medieval lanes of Josefov, Prague's historic Jewish Quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Charles Bridge for panoramic Vltava River views, then ascend to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) – the largest ancient castle complex in the world. With your private guide, tour St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and the Golden Lane. Enjoy a curated commentary on Bohemian royal history.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the Prague skyline (e.g., T-Anker or Cloud 9 Sky Bar). Followed by a fine-dining dinner at a Michelin-recognized Prague restaurant such as La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise – celebrated for its modern Czech tasting menus with wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast buffet or à la carte – fresh pastries, smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Café Savoy in Malá Strana – Art Nouveau interiors, Czech classics like svíčková and Bohemian pastries
meals.dinner: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise – 6- or 11-course Czech heritage tasting menu with paired wines (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Book Prague Castle private tour and La Degustation well in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes for cobblestone streets. September weather in Prague is typically mild (15–20°C), so bring a light jacket for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Private morning visit to the Lobkowicz Palace within Prague Castle complex – home to an extraordinary private art collection including original Beethoven and Mozart manuscripts. Enjoy a curator-led exclusive tour. Afterward, explore the charming Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood, including the Baroque Wallenstein Garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mucha Museum dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha, then browse the luxury boutiques and galleries of Pařížská Street (Prague's answer to the Champs-Élysées). In the late afternoon, take a private 90-minute Vltava River cruise on a premium yacht with champagne service, capturing golden-hour views of Prague's bridges and castle.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a world-class classical music concert – Prague is renowned for its musical heritage. Options include a performance at the Estates Theatre (where Mozart premiered Don Giovanni) or the Rudolfinum concert hall. Pre- and post-concert drinks at the hotel's cocktail lounge.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Eska – a celebrated modern Czech bistro in the Karlín district, known for sourdough, seasonal produce, and natural wines
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Alcron Restaurant (Radisson Blu Alcron Hotel) – Art Deco elegance, exceptional seafood and European fine dining

day_by_day.notes: Book concert tickets and river cruise in advance. The Estates Theatre is a short walk from Old Town – one of Europe's most beautiful opera houses. Dress code for the concert: smart elegant.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the striking Dancing House (Tančící dům) and a walk along the Vltava embankment. Then head to Vyšehrad, Prague's second historic castle complex, for breathtaking city panoramas, the Basilica of St. Peter and St. Paul, and the Vyšehrad Cemetery where Czech luminaries including Dvořák are buried. A quieter, more local experience away from the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Prague by private luxury transfer (approximately 2.5–3 hours) to Budapest, Hungary. Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside en route. Alternatively, opt for a premium first-class train on the EuroCity service for a stylish rail experience. Arrive in Budapest and check in to your luxury accommodation in the heart of the city.
day_by_day.evening: First impressions of Budapest: an evening stroll along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side, admiring the illuminated Buda Castle, Chain Bridge, and Hungarian Parliament Building – among the most spectacular urban nightscapes in Europe. Light welcome dinner at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Final Prague hotel breakfast – enjoy at leisure before checkout
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic hamper prepared by the hotel for the journey, or stop at a premium roadside restaurant in the Czech/Slovak countryside
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kollázs Brasserie & Bar (Four Seasons Gresham Palace, Budapest) – stunning Art Nouveau setting on the Danube, contemporary European cuisine

day_by_day.notes: This is the transition day between Prague and Budapest. Confirm private transfer or first-class rail booking well in advance. Luggage handling coordinated through your concierge. Budapest accommodation check-in typically from 15:00.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Buda Castle District (Castle Hill). Visit the Royal Palace (housing the Hungarian National Gallery), the Gothic Matthias Church with its stunning Zsolnay tile roof, and the Fisherman's Bastion – offering arguably the finest panoramic views in Budapest over the Danube and Pest. Explore the medieval streets and baroque architecture of this UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Széchenyi Chain Bridge to the Pest side. Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building on a private guided tour – one of Europe's largest and most ornate parliament buildings, featuring the Hungarian Holy Crown. Stroll through the elegant Lipótváros (Leopold Town) district. Late afternoon, visit the Great Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok) for premium Hungarian delicacies, fine paprika, Tokaji wine, and handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's legendary thermal bath culture: book an exclusive evening session at the Széchenyi or Gellért Thermal Baths (private cabin or VIP access). Afterward, a sophisticated dinner at Costes Downtown – Budapest's Michelin-starred restaurant offering innovative Hungarian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Alabárdos Restaurant in the Buda Castle District – medieval setting, traditional Hungarian cuisine elevated to fine dining
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown – Michelin-starred, contemporary Hungarian tasting menu with exceptional wine pairings (advance reservation required)

day_by_day.notes: Fisherman's Bastion is magical at sunrise and sunset – consider timing your visit accordingly. Book Costes Downtown well in advance as it is one of Budapest's most sought-after reservations. September in Budapest: 18–24°C, pleasant and ideal for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the awe-inspiring Hungarian State Opera House on a private behind-the-scenes tour – one of the world's most beautiful opera houses, rivaling Vienna's. Explore the gilded interiors, royal box, and stage. Afterward, walk the elegant Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's Champs-Élysées, UNESCO-listed) to Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the Millennium Monument, celebrating 1,000 years of Hungarian history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Museum of Fine Arts adjacent to Heroes' Square – housing one of Central Europe's finest collections of European masters including El Greco, Raphael, and Rembrandt. Late afternoon, wander through the romantic City Park (Városliget) and visit the fairy-tale Vajdahunyad Castle, a stunning architectural collage built for the 1896 Millennium Exhibition.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury private dinner cruise on the Danube River – enjoy a gourmet Hungarian dinner aboard a premium vessel as you glide past the illuminated Parliament, Buda Castle, and all seven bridges of Budapest. A truly unforgettable evening on the water.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Gerbeaud – Budapest's most iconic and historic café on Vörösmarty Square, established 1858. Enjoy traditional Hungarian pastries, cakes, and light dishes
meals.dinner: Private Danube dinner cruise with gourmet Hungarian cuisine, live traditional music, and premium wine service

day_by_day.notes: Book the Danube dinner cruise and Opera House tour in advance. Sunday in Budapest can see some attractions busier – the private tour format helps bypass queues. Andrássy Avenue is perfect for luxury shopping (Hermès, Louis Vuitton, local designers).

day_by_day.morning: Explore the historic Jewish Quarter of Budapest – home to the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street, the largest synagogue in Europe and second largest in the world. Take a moving private guided tour of the synagogue complex, the Jewish Museum, and the Memorial Garden of the Hungarian Jewish Martyrs. Then explore the vibrant ruin bars and bohemian street art of the 7th district (Erzsébetváros).
day_by_day.afternoon: Ascend Gellért Hill by private car or on foot for sweeping 360° panoramas of Budapest from the Citadella fortress. Visit the Liberty Statue (Szabadság-szobor). Descend to the Gellért Hotel & Thermal Baths – a magnificent Art Nouveau landmark – for an exclusive spa afternoon: thermal pools, steam rooms, and a premium massage treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House or the Liszt Academy of Music (Zeneakadémia) – a stunning Art Nouveau concert hall and one of the world's great music venues. Pre-performance champagne reception. Post-performance late dinner or dessert at a renowned Budapest patisserie.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Borkonyha Winekitchen – Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant in central Pest, outstanding Hungarian wine list and seasonal cuisine
meals.dinner: Post-performance dinner at Onyx Restaurant – two Michelin stars, Hungary's most celebrated fine dining destination, modern Hungarian haute cuisine (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: The Gellért Spa can be booked for private or semi-private sessions. Onyx Restaurant requires reservations well in advance and has a smart dress code. The Liszt Academy is a world-class venue – check the September 2027 program for performances.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure – sleep in and enjoy a long, indulgent hotel breakfast. Optional: a peaceful morning walk along the Danube Promenade or a final visit to a favorite spot. Consider a private cooking class or wine tasting session focused on Tokaji Aszú – Hungary's legendary 'wine of kings' – arranged through the hotel concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping on Váci Street or Andrássy Avenue – pick up fine Hungarian porcelain (Herend or Zsolnay), premium Tokaji wines, handmade leather goods, or Hungarian linen. Enjoy a farewell coffee and cake at New York Café – one of the world's most beautiful cafés, a gilded Belle Époque masterpiece. Private transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. Reflect on an extraordinary journey through two of Europe's most magnificent capitals – Prague and Budapest – a trip rich in imperial history, architectural splendor, world-class cuisine, and cultural treasures.

meals.breakfast: Lavish final hotel breakfast – treat yourself to the full spread
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Café New York (New York Palace Hotel) – legendary Belle Époque grandeur, Hungarian and European classics in one of the world's most stunning dining rooms
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight (depending on departure time)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for Budapest airport. The hotel concierge can arrange a premium private transfer. Consider purchasing Herend porcelain or Tokaji wine as premium gifts – both are quintessentially Hungarian luxury souvenirs. Confirm all departure logistics the evening before.
